subject: Data Structures through C
text: Which principle governs insertion and deletion in a stack?
explanation: A stack is last-in, first-out: the most recently pushed item is the first one popped.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: Which principle governs a standard queue?
explanation: A queue is first-in, first-out: the first item inserted is the first item removed.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search on a sorted array?
explanation: Each comparison halves the remaining search interval, giving logarithmic time complexity.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: What is the time complexity of inserting a node at the head of a singly linked list when the head pointer is available?
explanation: The new node only needs its next pointer set and the head pointer updated; no traversal is required.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: In an array-based circular queue that reserves one slot to distinguish full from empty, which condition indicates that the queue is full?
explanation: Advancing rear by one circular position would collide with front, so the queue is full.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: Which sequence describes preorder traversal of a binary tree?
explanation: Preorder visits the root first, then recursively visits the left subtree and the right subtree.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: If all keys in a binary search tree are distinct, what order does an inorder traversal produce?
explanation: Inorder traversal visits left subtree, node, then right subtree; the binary-search-tree ordering makes the result ascending.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: What is the worst-case time complexity of merge sort on n elements?
explanation: Merge sort divides the input into logarithmically many levels and performs O(n) merging work per level.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: What is the worst-case time complexity of linear search in an unsorted array of n elements?
explanation: In the worst case, every element must be checked before the target is found or absence is confirmed.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: Which data structure is primarily used by a typical program to manage active recursive function calls?
explanation: Each active function call stores its return address and local execution state in a stack frame.
